issuer: the Licensing Authority (the Government's Transport office)
note: Read 2026-10-31. The Government of Saint Lucia's portal, 'Apply for Driver's License' (office: Transport), says the applicant must be at least 18 and, for a new licence, submits the theory and practical test results with the fee. The Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic Act, s. 28(4), in the Revised Laws of Saint Lucia (2023) on the Attorney General's Chambers' site: a driver's licence is valid one year in the case of a first licence and three years for subsequent licences, and renewing the first licence needs a defensive driving course (s. 28(5)). The Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic (Fees) Regulations, as revised to 2023 (S.I. 42/2003 as amended to S.I. 81/2016), schedule: issue of a provisional one-year driver's licence EC$150; renewal of a driver's licence for one year EC$150, two years EC$250, three years EC$300. From is my reading: 18 plus the provisional first licence's one year, the full licence being the renewal after it (as Malaysia's and Algeria's are read). The terms are the Regulations' three renewal terms; the Act's s. 28(4)(b) says three years for subsequent licences, so the one- and two-year renewals stand on the Regulations alone. The portal gives EC$300 as the fee of its licence service, which matches the three-year renewal, not the provisional licence's EC$150. The test fees (EC$50 each) and the learner's permit aren't held. No identity card is held.
